questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: For f(x)=e^(2x)+3, with x real, determine f⁻¹, give its domain and verify your result by composition. [5 marks]
markPoints: Write y−3=e^(2x) after swapping the subject of the original function.
Take natural logarithms to obtain ln(y−3)=2x.
Therefore f⁻¹(x)=½ln(x−3).
The inverse has domain x>3, the original function's range.
Check f(f⁻¹(x))=e^[ln(x−3)]+3=x for x>3.
questions.modelAnswer: Write y−3=e^(2x) after swapping the subject of the original function. Take natural logarithms to obtain ln(y−3)=2x. Therefore f⁻¹(x)=½ln(x−3). The inverse has domain x>3, the original function's range. Check f(f⁻¹(x))=e^[ln(x−3)]+3=x for x>3.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Express (6x²−x+3)/(2x+1) as a linear expression plus one proper fraction. State the excluded value of x. [5 marks]
markPoints: Divide leading terms to obtain the first quotient term 3x.
Subtract (2x+1)(3x)=6x²+3x to leave −4x+3.
Divide the new leading term by 2x to obtain quotient term −2.
Subtract (2x+1)(−2)=−4x−2 to leave remainder 5.
Hence the expression is 3x−2+5/(2x+1), where x≠−½.
questions.modelAnswer: Divide leading terms to obtain the first quotient term 3x. Subtract (2x+1)(3x)=6x²+3x to leave −4x+3. Divide the new leading term by 2x to obtain quotient term −2. Subtract (2x+1)(−2)=−4x−2 to leave remainder 5. Hence the expression is 3x−2+5/(2x+1), where x≠−½.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Let f(x)=x(x−2)(x−5). Describe and sketch g(x)=f(−2x), labelling all intercepts and the end behaviour. [5 marks]
markPoints: The original graph has roots x=0, 2 and 5.
The input −2x reflects the graph in the y-axis.
It also scales horizontal distances by a factor ½.
The transformed x-intercepts are 0, −1 and −5/2.
The leading term of g is −8x³, so the graph rises to the left and falls to the right, crossing each simple root.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A sequence has u₁=5 and uₙ₊₁=−15/uₙ. Find its period and the sum of its first 103 terms. [4 marks]
markPoints: The terms repeat in pairs (5,−3), so the period is 2.
There are 51 complete pairs and one extra 5, giving S₁₀₃=51(5−3)+5=107.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Show that 2n³+5n²+5n+6 cannot be prime for any positive integer n. [5 marks]
markPoints: Define P(x)=2x³+5x²+5x+6 and evaluate P(−2)=0.
By the factor theorem, x+2 is a factor.
Division gives P(x)=(x+2)(2x²+x+3).
For every integer n≥1, n+2≥3 and 2n²+n+3≥6; both are integers greater than 1.
Thus P(n) is a product of two non-unit positive integers and is composite.
questions.modelAnswer: Define P(x)=2x³+5x²+5x+6 and evaluate P(−2)=0. By the factor theorem, x+2 is a factor. Division gives P(x)=(x+2)(2x²+x+3). For every integer n≥1, n+2≥3 and 2n²+n+3≥6; both are integers greater than 1. Thus P(n) is a product of two non-unit positive integers and is composite.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Solve 2sin(2θ)cosecθ+cos(2θ)secθ=5 for 0°≤θ≤360°. Explain which algebraic solutions must be discarded. [6 marks]
markPoints: Use sin(2θ)=2sinθcosθ and cos(2θ)=2cos²θ−1, noting sinθ≠0 and cosθ≠0.
Simplify the left side to 6cosθ−secθ.
Put u=cosθ and multiply by u to get 6u²−5u−1=0.
Factor (6u+1)(u−1)=0, giving u=−1/6 or u=1.
Reject u=1 because θ=0° or 360° makes cosecθ undefined.
For u=−1/6, θ≈99.6° or 260.4°, both valid.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Let f(x)=|x−3|+2 and g(x)=ln x. Find the range of f, the domain of g and h=g∘f. Explain why h lacks an inverse on R. Then restrict to x≥3 and find the inverse of h. [6 marks]
markPoints: The range of f is [2,∞).
The natural-log function g has domain (0,∞).
The composition is h(x)=ln(|x−3|+2), defined for every real x.
For example h(2)=h(4)=ln3, with two different inputs giving the same output.
Therefore h is not one-to-one on R and has no inverse function there.
On x≥3, h(x)=ln(x−1), so the inverse is h⁻¹(x)=1+e^x, with domain x≥ln2.
questions.modelAnswer: The range of f is [2,∞). The natural-log function g has domain (0,∞). The composition is h(x)=ln(|x−3|+2), defined for every real x. For example h(2)=h(4)=ln3, with two different inputs giving the same output. Therefore h is not one-to-one on R and has no inverse function there. On x≥3, h(x)=ln(x−1), so the inverse is h⁻¹(x)=1+e^x, with domain x≥ln2.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Evaluate exactly ∫ from x=0 to x=8/3 of (6x+1)/√(3x+1) dx by using a substitution and changing the limits. [7 marks]
markPoints: Choose u=3x+1.
Differentiate to get du=3dx, hence dx=du/3.
Rewrite 6x+1 as 2u−1.
Change the limits to u=1 when x=0 and u=9 when x=8/3.
The integral becomes (1/3)∫₁⁹(2u^(1/2)−u^(−1/2))du.
Integrate to obtain [(4/9)u^(3/2)−(2/3)u^(1/2)]₁⁹.
Substituting both limits gives (12−2)−(4/9−2/3)=10+2/9=92/9.
questions.modelAnswer: Choose u=3x+1. Differentiate to get du=3dx, hence dx=du/3. Rewrite 6x+1 as 2u−1. Change the limits to u=1 when x=0 and u=9 when x=8/3. The integral becomes (1/3)∫₁⁹(2u^(1/2)−u^(−1/2))du. Integrate to obtain [(4/9)u^(3/2)−(2/3)u^(1/2)]₁⁹. Substituting both limits gives (12−2)−(4/9−2/3)=10+2/9=92/9.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A curve is given by y³e^x+4y−27x=k. It has a stationary point on the y-axis. Find k, showing the implicit differentiation. [6 marks]
markPoints: Differentiate y³e^x by the product rule, obtaining e^x(3y²dy/dx+y³).
Differentiate the remaining terms to obtain 4dy/dx−27.
Therefore e^x(3y²dy/dx+y³)+4dy/dx−27=0.
At a stationary point on the y-axis, dy/dx=0 and x=0.
The derivative equation reduces to y³−27=0, so y=3.
Substitute x=0 and y=3 into the curve: k=27+12=39.
questions.modelAnswer: Differentiate y³e^x by the product rule, obtaining e^x(3y²dy/dx+y³). Differentiate the remaining terms to obtain 4dy/dx−27. Therefore e^x(3y²dy/dx+y³)+4dy/dx−27=0. At a stationary point on the y-axis, dy/dx=0 and x=0. The derivative equation reduces to y³−27=0, so y=3. Substitute x=0 and y=3 into the curve: k=27+12=39.

questions.prompt: Consider f(x)=x³−3x−1 and the iteration xₙ₊₁=(3xₙ+1)^(1/3), beginning with x₁=1. Show a root lies between 1 and 2, then calculate x₂, x₃ and x₄ to four decimal places. [4 marks]
markPoints: f(1)=−3 and f(2)=1, so there is a sign change and a root lies in (1,2).
Substitute x₁=1 into the given recurrence to find x₂=1.5874.
Substitute x₂ into the recurrence to obtain x₃=1.7928.
Substitute x₃ into the recurrence to obtain x₄=1.8545.
